clusterfuzzlite/build.candidate: The ClusterFuzzLite build compiles fuzz_config_parser.c with the fuzzing engine's compiler and flags into a fuzz_config_parser binary in the output directory

clusterfuzzlite/dockerfile.candidate: The fuzzing build image starts from the OSS-Fuzz base-builder image
The repository is copied into $SRC/nginx-lua and used as the working directory
The ClusterFuzzLite build script is placed at $SRC/build.sh for the fuzz build to run

clusterfuzzlite/fuzz-config-parser.candidate: The fuzz harness picks one of three parsers (directive name, size value, listen address) based on the first input byte, and ignores inputs shorter than 2 bytes
A directive name that starts with a digit is rejected, and the name ends at ';', '{', '}' or a NUL byte

Size values such as '10m' or '256k' use k/m/g suffixes as multiples of 1024; input is cut off at 63 bytes; 'g' multiplication can overflow a signed long (undefined behaviour the harness itself would trigger)
A listen address is accepted as a plain port or host:port with port 0-65535; a host:port with an empty or non-numeric port is accepted as port 0
Fuzzing nginx-lua configuration parsing finds crashes in directive, size and listen handling

Multi-stage copy of only selected builder paths into the final image
apk upgrade of all packages at build time
Smoke test of envsubst, nginx -V/-t, luajit, lua, luarocks during build
Compiled-in paths (prefix, pid, lock, temp paths, modules path)
Official-image compatibility env vars NGINX_VERSION, NJS_VERSION, PKG_RELEASE
Version pins for every bundled resty library
Installation of bundled resty libraries (redis, mysql, cookie, ...)
